content:
Was re-reading Melanie Mitchell's 2019 book, "Artificial Intelligence: A Guide for Thinking Humans", https://melaniemitchell.me/aibook/ and was relieved to (re)read how she refers to "units" instead of "neurons" in artificial neural networks. Even adds a note about doing so to avoid the dismay of neuroscientists. Indeed.

Got reminded again today of how powerful biological neurons are by Mickey London's lab latest preprint:

"What can a neuron compute", Aizenbud et al. 2026 (Segev, London)
https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.06.08.730984v1.full

The secret sauce of biological neurons? Mostly dendritic morphology:

"Bounds on the computational complexity of neurons due to dendritic morphology"
Anamika Agrawal, Michael A. Buice 2025
https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.07.11.664448v1

A point spectacularly well made by Jones and Kording a while back:

"Can single neurons solve MNIST? the computational power of biological dendritic trees", Jones and Kording 2020
https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.01269

... in line with plenty of prior work, even by the same lab, like:

"On Functions Computed on Trees", Farhoodi et al. 2019
https://direct.mit.edu/neco/article/31/11/2075/95669/On-Functions-Computed-on-Trees

The key ingredient? That a presynaptic neuron delivers multiple inputs across the postsynaptic neuron's dendritic tree. That enables a lot of the above's computational properties. To reproduce that, a whole multi-layer ANN is needed to match the power of a single cortical pyramidal neuron:

"Single cortical neurons as deep artificial neural networks", Beniaguev, Segev, London 2021.
https://www.cell.com/neuron/fulltext/S0896-6273(21)00501-8

What's more, adding biological constraints to ANNs improve the latter:

"Do Biological Constraints Impair Dendritic Computation?", Jones and Kording 2021
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306452221003900

#neuroscience #dendrites #ANN #AI
